scope: Native erlang:is_atom/1. Existing X/Y atom guards and constant-literal lowering are reused; no new instruction family is admitted.
adaptations: Charge one bounded native step and use the native atom tag test. Booleans and ordinary atoms return true; NIL, numbers and other term classes return false. No allocation, collection or truthiness conversion occurs.
Add only is_atom/1 to the positive plain-BIF whitelist. The existing nonallocating native BIF groups preserve work-failure precedence; existing atom guards already implement X/Y and literal forms.

Extend the shared predicate harness with an explicit atom mode and false/ordinary-atom samples, retaining integer/list regression modes. Independent OTP answers cover boolean and ordinary atoms, NIL versus atoms, other term classes, body/X/Y guards, and constant-literal guards.

Force GC in the allocation following an accepted guard, without claiming the predicate itself allocates. Exercise allocation prefixes, callback OOM versus memory denial, work prefixes for true/false/NIL outcomes, value preservation and shared-worker exact bytes/budgets/reuse/peers/reclamation.
